Updated assessment using the Financial Stability Report (FSR) as context:
- Policy tone remains dovish-leaning: a 50 bp cut, “greater confidence” that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2%, and “risks…roughly in balance,” plus lower IORB (4.9%) and ON RRP (4.8%), all ease front-end conditions.
- FSR tempering factors: vulnerabilities in money market funds and other nonbanks to funding risks; continued balance-sheet runoff keeps Treasury supply elevated, and the FSR notes term premia and long rates are sensitive to supply and inflation, alongside risks of market-liquidity strains and foreign divestment from U.S. assets. CRE stresses and leverage buildup remain watchpoints. These reduce how “risk-friendly” the cut is, even as some securitization segments have recovered in 2024.
Net: still moderately positive for financial conditions and risk assets, but more cautious than a pure dovish read given Treasury market and nonbank vulnerabilities, ongoing QT, and liquidity risk highlighted in the FSR.
